To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the carbon footprint (CF), as a part of the life cycle assessment (LC), of N containing fertilizer is a very complex and challenging problem; (2) the CF of the fertilizer technology is determined by a combination of the production and use stages, and (3) it is possible to include the carbon sequestration in soil and plants into the CF balance sheet, thus, reducing the CF by 87.6%.
the inclusion of the CO2 assimilation into the LCA balance sheet reduces the CF of fertilizer technologies by about 90%.
the inclusion of CO 2 assimilation by the plants into the balance sheet offsets 86.6% of carbon footprint (CF).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of environmental impact (i.e. CF) of N containing fertilizer technology.
the development of the new methodology for LCA of fertilizer technologies.
the assessment of environmental impact and life cycle costs for various fertilizer technologies in the context of the EU Fertilizers Regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LCA approach is the only way of a reliable determination of the CF of fertilizer technologies.
the CF of fertilizer production and its use is not a major problem.
the LCA based CF of N fertilizer technologies should be determined with the inclusion of the CO2 assimilation during vegetation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CF of fertilizer technology is a complex issue, which should be considered as a whole.
the CF of fertilizer production and its use is not as high as it was thought.
the LCA based CF determination is a promising approach to evaluate the environmental performance of fertilizer technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of the CO2 assimilation in balance sheet is a necessary step for more accurate determination of CF of fertilizer technologies.
the inclusion of the CO2 assimilation into the balance sheet is a necessary condition for a reliable assessment of fertilizer technologies.
the CF of fertilizer production and use can be reduced by 87.6%, which is a very promising result.
